encounters.cc: Progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue over the past three months.

lines: Progressive exertional dyspnea and fatigue over the past three months.
He reports a 3-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea and orthopnea.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
- Status post ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement
His medications include aspirin, metoprolol, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Father: Coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction at age 62
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Retired postal service worker.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla.
An echocardiogram reveals a dilated left ventricle with an area of akinesis in the anterior wall and septum, and a reduced ejection fraction of 35%.
An ECG shows persistent ST-segment elevation in the anterior leads and deep Q waves.

encounters.cc: Worsening shortness of breath over the past two days with orthopnea and lower extremity edema.

lines: Worsening shortness of breath over the past two days with orthopnea and lower extremity edema.

The patient with ischemic cardiomyopathy and left ventricular aneurysm, last evaluated six months ago for progressive dyspnea, reports that he now feels winded walking across his bedroom and has had to sleep upright in a chair the past two nights due to breathlessness when lying down.
He has also noticed swelling in his feet and lower legs.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular aneurysm (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
- Status post ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
His medical history includes coronary artery disease with a prior myocardial infarction, chronic systolic heart failure, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement
He admits to running out of his medications, including furosemide and lisinopril, about a week ago.
- Father: Coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction at age 62
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension
He does not smoke or drink alcohol.
His blood pressure is 102/68 mm Hg, heart rate is 106/min, and respiratory rate is 26/min.
On examination, he appears tired and mildly confused.
Jugular venous distension is noted to the angle of the mandible.
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral crackles throughout the lung bases.
Cardiac exam shows a laterally displaced apical impulse and an S3 gallop.
There is moderate pitting edema in both lower extremities.
Chest x-ray reveals an enlarged cardiac silhouette with pulmonary vascular congestion and Kerley B lines.
ECG shows sinus tachycardia with Q waves in the inferior leads.
He is placed on oxygen and intravenous diuretics.
A pulmonary artery catheter is inserted to assess hemodynamics.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset severe shortness of breath and progressive ankle swelling over the past week.

lines: Sudden onset severe shortness of breath and progressive ankle swelling over the past week.

68-year-old male with ischemic cardiomyopathy and left ventricular aneurysm, returning with similar symptoms, presents with severe shortness of breath that developed suddenly over the past several hours.
He reports progressive swelling of his ankles over the last week and recent difficulty lying flat at night.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular aneurysm (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Status post ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
He has a history of long-standing hypertension and coronary artery disease, and he was recently hospitalized for a myocardial infarction.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement
- Father: Coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction at age 62
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Retired postal service worker.
Respiratory rate of 32/min and oxygen saturation of 86% on room air.
Blood pressure is 168/102 mm Hg, and heart rate is 112/min.
On examination, he appears anxious and diaphoretic.
Jugular venous distension is present, and auscultation of the chest reveals diffuse crackles bilaterally.
Cardiac examination shows a third heart sound.
Chest x-ray demonstrates diffuse alveolar infiltrates and bilateral pleural effusions.
Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema
Treatment is started with nesiritide, a drug that is structurally identical to endogenous human B-type natriuretic peptide.

encounters.cc: Acute confusion and disorientation noted by neighbor, with reduced oral intake due to nocturia.

lines: Acute confusion and disorientation noted by neighbor, with reduced oral intake due to nocturia.

The patient is a 69-year-old male with ischemic cardiomyopathy and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction previously evaluated in 2020 and 2021 for cardiac decompensation, now presenting with acute confusion.
He is disoriented to time and place but able to state his name.
He has no family with him and appears to have difficulty recalling his medical history.
His neighbor reports he has been drinking less water lately due to fear of going to the bathroom at night.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular aneurysm (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Status post ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Father: Coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction at age 62
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension
The patient has no advance directive or designated surrogate decision-maker on file.
On examination, his blood pressure is 160/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F)
His skin is warm and dry. Neurological examination reveals no focal deficits.

encounters.cc: Found unresponsive at home after earlier complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath.

lines: Found unresponsive at home after earlier complaints of chest pain and shortness of breath.
The patient is a 70-year-old male with coronary artery disease, hypertension, and progressive ischemic cardiomyopathy following left ventricular aneurysm with recurrent heart failure exacerbations.
He is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after his wife found him unresponsive at home.
His wife reports that he complained of shortness of breath and chest pain earlier in the day but refused to seek medical attention.
- Ischemic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular aneurysm (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (diagnosed 2020-07-15)
- Status post ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement
He takes aspirin, metoprolol, and metformin.
- Father: Coronary artery disease with myocardial infarction at age 62
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: No alcohol use. Occupation: Retired postal service worker.
On arrival, he is pulseless and apneic.
The cardiac monitor shows organized electrical activity without a detectable pulse.
His initial laboratory values are as follows:
- Arterial blood gas (on 100% O2): pH 7.1, PaCO2 60 mmHg, PaO2 500 mmHg
The patient is intubated, and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is initiated.
An intravenous line is established, and epinephrine is administered.
